# n4 - Migration, the roadmap-graph command, and packaging

`RoadmapMigration.derive(path)` reads a graphless roadmap's existing batch order and returns the
conservative edge set: every entry of batch N needs every entry of batch N-1, and batch 1 needs
nothing. `scripts/roadmap-graph` exposes three verbs over n1, n3, and this module: `check`,
`render`, and `migrate`, every verb honouring `--dry-run`. This node also registers the new
scripts and libraries in the `CORE_FILES` manifest, without which the suite goes red the moment
the command exists.

## n4 failure-mode matrix
| Row | Operation | Failure mode | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1 | Derive batch 1 as roots | Batch 1 entries are given an edge to a batch that does not exist, and the derived graph is dangling on every roadmap the migration touches | `roadmap_migration_test#test_first_batch_entries_need_nothing` |
| 4.2 | Make batch N need every entry of batch N-1 | Only the first entry of the previous batch becomes a need, so parallel work in that batch is not a blocker and the migration weakens the order it was meant to preserve | `roadmap_migration_test#test_batch_n_needs_every_entry_of_the_previous_batch` |
| 4.3 | Never overwrite an existing `## Graph` | The owner's hand-edited edges are replaced by a derived guess, silently destroying the only place a cross-intent edge lives | `roadmap_migration_test#test_existing_graph_is_left_untouched_and_reported_as_skipped` |
| 4.4 | Migrate idempotently | A second migration rewrites the section and the owner's later edits are lost on the next run | `roadmap_migration_test#test_migrating_twice_changes_no_bytes_the_second_time` |
| 4.5 | Cycle check the derived graph before writing | A malformed batch list produces a cyclic derivation that is written to disk unchecked | `roadmap_migration_test#test_derived_graph_is_cycle_checked_before_write` |
| 4.6 | Derive from a legacy `## Waves` heading | The seven pre-ruling roadmaps derive an empty graph and stay graphless forever | `roadmap_migration_test#test_waves_heading_derives_the_same_edges_as_batches` |
| 4.7 | Handle a roadmap with a single batch | The derivation emits no `## Graph` at all, or one with no lines, and the roadmap is left in the state the migration was supposed to end | `roadmap_migration_test#test_single_batch_roadmap_derives_all_roots` |
| 4.8 | Keep a delivered entry as a need | A delivered entry is dropped from the derivation, so the entries that needed it become roots and read as ready before their real predecessor | `roadmap_migration_test#test_delivered_entries_still_appear_as_needs` |
| 4.9 | `check` a cyclic roadmap from the CLI | The command exits 0 on a broken roadmap, so no script or hook can gate on it | `roadmap_graph_cli_test#test_check_on_a_cyclic_roadmap_exits_1_with_the_path` |
| 4.10 | Honour `--dry-run` on every verb | A dry run writes to disk, so the only safe way to preview a migration across twenty-three live files is not safe | `roadmap_graph_cli_test#test_dry_run_writes_nothing_and_prints_the_diff` |
| 4.11 | Refuse a missing or non-roadmap path | The command prints a Ruby backtrace instead of a reason, and a typo looks like a code failure | `roadmap_graph_cli_test#test_unknown_path_exits_with_a_named_reason_not_a_backtrace` |
| 4.12 | Refuse an unknown verb and no argument | The command silently does nothing, or does the wrong verb, when called by a script with a stale flag | `roadmap_graph_cli_test#test_no_argument_exits_2_and_unknown_verb_exits_2` |
| 4.13 | Exit non-zero when `check` finds a dangling need | A graph naming an id no batch lists passes the check, so the one command that could catch a bad hand edit does not | `roadmap_graph_cli_test#test_check_exits_1_when_the_graph_names_an_unlisted_id` |
| 4.14 | Register every new script and library in `CORE_FILES` | Folded at review (B1): `install_sync_test#test_every_required_lib_is_distributed` scans every file under `scripts/`, so the suite goes red the instant `scripts/roadmap-graph` requires an unregistered lib, and an installed Plastic would raise `LoadError` at boot | `roadmap_graph_cli_test#test_new_scripts_and_libs_are_registered_in_core_files` |
| 4.15 | Refuse a heading that begins `## Graph` without being exactly `## Graph` | Folded at review (A9, D13): `chat-shell-maturity.md` carries a thirty-line superseded graph note under such a heading. The exact-match reader cannot see it, so `migrate` would write a second `## Graph` beside it | `roadmap_migration_test#test_migrate_refuses_a_roadmap_carrying_a_graph_like_heading` |
| 4.16 | Emit one edge line per id when an id appears in two batches | Folded at review (A14): two declarations of one id are rejected by `GraphEdges.parse` as a duplicate and dropped, so the entry silently loses every edge it should have had | `roadmap_migration_test#test_id_listed_in_two_batches_yields_one_edge_line` |
| 4.17 | Skip an abandoned entry when deriving needs | Folded at review (A10, D15): an abandoned entry in an early batch becomes a need nothing can ever satisfy, and every entry behind it is blocked forever with no reason in the payload | `roadmap_migration_test#test_abandoned_entry_is_not_derived_as_a_need` |

## Steps
1. Red: the matrix's tests above, committed before any code in this node.
2. Write the code that makes them pass.
3. Green, then `ruby bin/test` at its baseline before the next node starts.
